newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian aluminium boss says can clear his name.
newsitem.headline: Russian aluminium boss says can clear his name.

text.p: A senior Russian aluminium official under investigation for alleged financial misdemeanours has evidence to clear his name, a Moscow representative of his company said on Thursday.

Economic crime officials said last month they were investigating Yuri Kolpakov, general director of Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter, over an alleged failure to repatriate $20 million to the firm from raw material supply contracts.
"From our point of view, there was no crime here," said Georgy Pashkov, director of the smelter's Moscow representation.
Kolpakov has paid the money into the company's accounts and appealed to Russia's prosecutor general, Yuri Skuratov, to clear his name, Pashkov told Reuters in an interview.
A bank statement, dated June 30 and seen by Reuters, shows $21,484,365 were paid to the Krasnoyarsk Aluminium Smelting Company by an offshore concern called Leo Trust Company.
In a written appeal, Kolpakov said there had been no crime.
"It will become clear that this case should be dropped because of the absence of any criminal act," Kolpakov said.
There was no immediate response from the investigators.
In his appeal, Kolpakov said Krasnoyarsk paid $20 million in mid-1996 to Leo for raw materials Leo was to have supplied to the smelter under a tolling deal.
Tolling deals, which account for the bulk of Russia's aluminium output, work on the basis of a trading company supplying a smelter with raw materials and then exporting the finished product.
But the deal fell through after delivery delays and changes in market conditions which meant the original contract was no longer profitable for the smelter, Kolpakov said.
Leo returned the money, plus interest, to the smelter, and it is this sum which Kolpakov allegedly failed to return.
Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov is locked in a battle against what he has called the "crime-ridden" world of Russian aluminium.
Russia is the world's largest exporter of the metal, which is used in applications ranging from packaging to engine parts.

Production last year hit 2.87 million tonnes of which Krasnoyarsk produced 770,000, or 27 percent of the total. Exports were 2.44 million tonnes and were up around two percent year-on-year in the first four months of 1997.
Krasnoyarsk is the second largest aluminium plant in the world after neighbouring Siberian rival Bratsk
